home_story_1: Two months ago I read the blog post “{post}” by Stepan Parunashvili about turning an iPhone into a dumbphone with Apple Configurator. I tried it. The setup was fine; the effort is a part of why it holds. But that setup had some serious problems.
home_story_2: The App Store was off, so nothing updated. I couldn't log in to my bank app. The web was an allow list, so I could not even scan a QR menu at a restaurant. The configuration part is done via Apple Configurator manually by clicking buttons. I realized using Apple Configurator isn't even necessary. So I built a guide that keeps the App Store on, blocks the apps even if they're installed, blocks their URLs, and leaves the rest of the phone alone.
home_story_3: I met a lot of people lately. Per my observations, most of people's problems come down to not being able to do hard things. When I check their screen time I mostly saw 6 hours and more.
home_story_4: People do anything to escape the hard work. And having an infinite amusement machine on their fingertips makes this a thousand times easier.
home_story_5: I think I finally fixed this for myself and I wanted to turn my expertise into a non-profit social awareness project.
home_story_6: That is the whole reason this site exists. If more people try blocking these distracting apps, we could learn more, experiment more and share more.
home_story_7: I used the time I got from Instagram reels to build this website as the ultimate example.
home_story_8: We should get better at protecting ourselves and our next generations from a system built to farm attention.
home_story_9: It is not only the hours. It is what the hours do. You stop doing hard things. You stop getting better at anything. The muscle goes soft and you become a cog. I wanted a way out that does not depend on willpower, because mine runs out by afternoon like everyone else's.
home_story_10: Most people will close this tab. That is fine. This is for the ones who will be glad they found it, the way I was glad I found that blog post.
home_how_profile_body: A configuration profile is the file companies use to manage work phones. This site builds yours in the browser and signs it; nothing is uploaded. Yours can block apps by name so they never open even if downloaded, block websites in every browser, filter adult content, and lock itself so it stays.
home_how_supervision_body: Supervision is a device mode Apple built for schools and companies. A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: hiding apps, and a profile that cannot be removed. Apple's way to get there erases the phone; our guide does it from a backup and keeps everything. The whole setup takes about 45 minutes, plus a one-hour security delay on some iPhones.
home_how_app_body: Plug the iPhone in with a cable. The app backs it up, flips one flag inside the backup and restores it, and the phone comes back supervised with everything still on it. It takes about 45 minutes, erases nothing, costs nothing, and needs an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or newer.
home_faq_supervision_desc: A device mode Apple built for schools and companies. A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: hiding apps, and a profile that cannot be removed. Everything else about the phone stays the same.
home_faq_see_term: Can the supervisor see my phone?
home_faq_see_desc: No. Supervision is a flag, not a connection. Remote control needs an MDM server, and you enrol in none. The patch runs on your own Mac and sends nothing. The profile is a fixed file: once installed, nobody can change it or read anything back.
home_faq_erase_term: Do I have to erase my iPhone?
home_faq_erase_desc: No. Apple's way erases. Our guide supervises from a local backup: back up to a Mac, patch one flag, restore. Photos, messages and logins stay.
home_faq_data_desc: No. The supervision step patches a backup and restores it to the same phone. Apps re-download; an encrypted backup carries your saved passwords, Health data and keychain, so fewer of them ask you to log in again. Keep a local backup on your Mac anyway. It is faster than iCloud and you can restore it in one click.
home_faq_undo_desc: Yes. Remove the profile from Settings if the phone is not supervised. On a supervised phone, erasing the phone removes supervision; restore from iCloud or your local backup after.
home_faq_change_term: Can I change the profile later?
home_faq_change_desc: You can always add restrictions by installing another profile. You cannot loosen or remove one without erasing the phone. Start with the recommended list; add later if needed. Each download is a new profile; installing another one adds to what is already blocked. Want to try first? Turn on trial mode and the profile stays removable.
home_faq_updates_term: Will my banking apps keep updating?
home_faq_updates_desc: Yes. The App Store stays on. Only the apps you list disappear.
home_faq_keep_term: What about WhatsApp, Maps, my bank?
home_faq_keep_desc: Untouched. You choose the list. We only suggest the feeds.
home_faq_apple_desc: It uses Apple's own configuration profiles and backup format. The no-wipe supervision trick is not documented by Apple; it works on iOS 26.6.1 today.
home_faq_mac_desc: You need a Mac once, for about an hour. Borrow one. The profile needs no Mac afterwards.
home_faq_android_desc: Not yet. Android has no settings file like this; blocking that holds needs a small device-owner app, which is a different build. We plan to add it. Until then this site is iPhone only, and Digital Wellbeing limits still rely on your willpower.
home_faq_windows_term: Does it work from a Windows PC?
home_faq_windows_desc: Not yet. The supervision tool runs on a Mac today. Windows makes the same backup through iTunes, so support is planned. Until then, borrow a Mac once; the phone needs no computer afterwards.
home_faq_who_desc: Mert Duzgun, a developer in Antalya. This is not a business. The code is public, the profile is signed with my Apple developer certificate, and nothing you do here is tracked.

guide_sup_description: Supervision lets a configuration profile hide apps and refuse removal. Apple gets there by erasing the phone. This guide gets there from a backup and keeps your data.
guide_sup_intro: Supervision is a device mode Apple built for schools and companies, and it is the only way to hide apps and to install a profile that cannot be removed. Apple gets there by erasing the phone; this guide gets there from a backup, so everything on the iPhone stays where it is.
sup_head_title: Supervise your iPhone without erasing it
sup_title: Supervise your iPhone without erasing it
sup_lead: Supervision is a device mode Apple built for schools and companies. It is the only way to make a profile unremovable and to hide apps. Apple's official path wipes the phone. This guide keeps your data.
sup_get_apps: Apps you choose disappear and cannot open, even if they get downloaded again
sup_get_profile: The profile cannot be removed from Settings
sup_get_store: The App Store keeps working, so your apps keep updating
sup_get_rest: Everything else on the phone stays exactly as it is: photos, messages, apps, logins
sup_cost_time: About 45 minutes of your attention, plus up to an hour of waiting if the iPhone asks for a security delay before Stolen Device Protection turns off
sup_cost_mac: A Mac with a cable (Windows works with iTunes but our tool is Mac only for now)
sup_cost_redownload: Apps re-download from the App Store after the restore; a few ask you to log in again; Face ID needs to be set up again
sup_cost_findmy: Find My iPhone has to be off during the restore; you turn it back on after
sup_checklist_passcode: Know your iPhone passcode and your Apple account password
sup_checklist_stolen: Settings > Face ID & Passcode > turn off Stolen Device Protection first. If the iPhone shows a security delay, it is a one-hour wait, so do this step at home (a familiar location skips the delay on many phones) or start it an hour before you sit down
sup_checklist_findmy: Settings > your name > Find My > Find My iPhone > off
sup_checklist_backup: Recommended: a local backup on your Mac (Finder > Back Up Now). Faster than iCloud, one click to restore. iCloud backup as a second net if you have the space.
sup_checklist_space: On the Mac: free space equal to what the iPhone uses. A 64 gb phone with 40 gb in use needs about 40 gb free, because the backup is a full copy
sup_checklist_fulldisk: On the Mac: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > add your terminal app, then quit and reopen the terminal
sup_step1_title: Step 1: back up to your Mac
sup_step1_plug: Plug the iPhone into the Mac, unlock it, tap Trust
sup_step1_finder: Finder > your iPhone > General > "Back up all data on this iPhone to this Mac"
sup_step1_encrypt: Leave "Encrypt local backup" as it is. The tool handles both kinds of backup
sup_step1_run: Click Back Up Now. A 14 gb phone took about 9 minutes for us
sup_step1_why: Keep the backup encrypted if it already is: an encrypted backup carries your saved passwords, Health data and keychain, so more survives the restore. The tool asks for the backup password once and keeps nothing. An unencrypted backup works as well
sup_step2_body: The backup contains a small settings file named CloudConfigurationDetails.plist. It has one switch, IsSupervised, set to false. We set it to true and keep the file exactly the same size so the backup stays valid. Nothing else in the backup changes.
sup_step2_download: Install the tool with the first line below (with pipx instead: pipx install supervise-iphone)
sup_step2_check: check lists your backups: device, iOS version, encrypted yes/no, current flag
sup_step2_patch: patch shows the change, asks for confirmation, and keeps an untouched copy of the file next to your backups. On an encrypted backup it asks for the backup password first
sup_step2_unpatch: unpatch undoes the change, as long as you have not restored yet
sup_step2_commands:
curl -fsSL https://attentionawareness.com/install.sh | sh
supervise check
supervise patch
supervise unpatch

sup_step3_order: The order is not optional: Finder refuses to restore while Find My iPhone is on, and iOS refuses to turn Find My off while Stolen Device Protection is on. Stolen Device Protection, then Find My, then the restore
sup_step3_restore: Finder > your iPhone > Restore Backup > pick the backup you just made > Restore
sup_step3_reboot: The iPhone reboots, shows an "Upgrade" screen, asks for your passcode, then lands on the home screen
sup_step3_settings: Open Settings. The top of the page should read "This iPhone is supervised"
sup_step3_verify: Optional: verify asks the connected iPhone itself (needs Apple Configurator from the Mac App Store)
sup_step4_findmy: Turn Find My iPhone back on
sup_step4_setup: The iPhone runs a short setup: it asks you to set up Face ID or Touch ID again, to choose a passcode, and it offers to turn Stolen Device Protection back on. Say yes
sup_step4_apps: Then it downloads your apps again. The greyed-out icons take a few minutes, so keep the iPhone on wifi and on power
sup_step4_profile: Install your attentionawareness profile from the generator: AirDrop the file, Settings > Profile Downloaded > Install. Blocked apps vanish, sites are blocked, the profile shows as unremovable
sup_step4_stacks: Every download is its own profile: a later one stacks on top of the one before it instead of replacing it. Only erasing the phone takes them off
sup_verified_row_result: Supervised, all data kept, 5 hidden apps removed by cable afterwards
sup_verified_row_result_2: Encrypted backup, supervised, all data kept
sup_verified_earlier: Earlier community reports: iOS 15, 16 (Ask Different, 2023), iOS 17 encrypted via iMazing (2024)
sup_trouble_permission_term: "Operation not permitted" when the tool runs
sup_trouble_permission_desc: The terminal lacks Full Disk Access. Grant it, quit and reopen the terminal
sup_trouble_password_desc: It is the password you set in Finder for the backup, not your iPhone passcode
sup_trouble_unsupervised_desc: The restore probably used a different backup. Run check, confirm IsSupervised is true on the backup you restore, retry. Until the phone is supervised, installing the profile fails with "unsupervised devices require a contentfilteruuid"
sup_trouble_undo_desc: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Erase All Content and Settings removes supervision. Restore from your local or iCloud backup afterwards. This is the only way Apple gives to leave supervision
sup_notes_privacy: Nobody can see your phone. Supervision is a flag, not a connection: remote control needs an MDM server, and this enrols you in none. The patch runs on your own Mac and sends nothing. The profile is a fixed file of restrictions; once installed, nobody can change it or read anything back. The only thing this site ever receives is the list of apps and sites you chose, so it can sign the file
sup_notes_unsupported: This is not an Apple supported procedure. It uses the backup format, which Apple can change. It works on iOS 26.6.1 today
sup_notes_organization: Supervising with a Mac and no company MDM means the phone is "supervised by" whoever ran the tool; the organization name shows empty
sup_notes_roadmap: A Windows version is on the list
sup_alt_erase: Erase path: if you do not mind starting fresh, Apple Configurator's "Prepare" with "Supervise devices" ticked, then set the phone up as new
mac_description: The Mac app that turns your iPhone into a supervised iPhone without erasing it, and back. Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or newer, free and open source.
mac_lead: Turns your iPhone into a supervised iPhone without erasing it, and back. Plug in, click, wait.
mac_requirements: An Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 14 or newer, a cable, about 45 minutes. Free.
mac_download_notarized: Signed and notarized with Apple's Developer ID, so macOS opens it after the usual check. It is not in the App Store because it talks to your iPhone over the cable, which the store does not allow.
mac_step_connect: Connect. Plug the iPhone into the Mac and unlock it. The app waits until it sees the phone.
mac_step_checks: Checks. Find My off, Stolen Device Protection off, enough free space on the Mac, and the backup password if your backup is encrypted.
mac_step_backup: Back up. The app makes a full backup in its own folder. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
mac_step_patch: Patch. One flag inside that backup is set. An untouched copy of every file it writes is kept beside it.
mac_step_restore: Restore. The iPhone restarts and restores itself. Keep the cable in.
mac_step_profile: Profile. The app installs the profile you built on the {builder} over the cable.
mac_step_done: Done. The iPhone is supervised, your data is still on it, and the profile holds.
mac_steps_reverse: The same steps in reverse unsupervise the phone.
mac_honest_unsupported: Apple does not support this. It is a patch of a private file inside a backup, and Apple can change that format
mac_honest_no_erase: The phone is never erased. A restore puts your apps, photos, messages and settings back where they were
mac_honest_verified: Tested on an iPhone 16e class device on iOS 26.6.1 (2026-09-10, unencrypted backup) and on an iPhone SE on iOS 26.2.1 (2026-09-12, encrypted backup)
mac_honest_source: Open source at {repo}, in the folder apps/mac
mac_cli_body: The {guide} does the same thing, one command at a time.
mac_promo_title: There is a Mac app that does all of this
mac_promo_body: Plug in, click, wait. The {app} runs every step on this page for you.
ext_privacy_lead: The attention awareness extension hides feeds with CSS. It collects nothing.
ext_privacy_stores_body: Your switches (on or off per site) and the custom CSS rules you write, in the browser's extension storage.
ext_privacy_stores_sync: If you are signed into your browser, the browser may sync that storage across your devices. Nothing else.
ext_privacy_sends_body: Nothing. No analytics, no crash reports, no remote code, no network requests of its own.
ext_privacy_sees_body: The pages on x.com, youtube.com, instagram.com and tiktok.com, only to inject CSS.
ext_privacy_sees_custom: If you add a custom rule for another site, the browser asks you once for access to that site. The extension then injects your CSS there and nothing more.
ext_privacy_source_body: The code is public at {repo}, and the rules are plain CSS files you can read.
guide_ext_head_title: Use social media from your computer, not your phone
guide_ext_title: Use social media from your computer, not your phone
guide_ext_description: The phone is a slot machine in your pocket. A computer is a desk you get up from. The attention awareness extension cuts the feeds out of X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok so the browser stays a tool.
guide_ext_intro: The profile takes the apps off the iPhone. This is the other half: a browser extension that removes the feeds from the four sites that carry them, and leaves the rest of each site alone.
guide_ext_why_1: The phone is a slot machine in my pocket. It is always there, the feed is vertical, and one thumb runs it, so a minute of waiting turns into forty with no decision anywhere in the middle.
guide_ext_why_2: A computer is a desk. I sit down at it, I do the thing I came for, and then I get up and leave. Same accounts, same people, same posts, but the room has a door.
guide_ext_why_3: Once the apps are blocked on the iPhone, the computer is where I still post, message, search and watch the channels I chose. The extension cuts the feeds out of the four sites so the computer stays a tool rather than the phone with a bigger screen. Those are the same hours a day {receipt} bills you for over the next twenty years.
guide_ext_why_receipt_link: the receipt on the home page
guide_ext_install_body: Chrome, Brave, Edge, any Chromium browser. It is not in a store yet, so it loads from a folder. One minute.
guide_ext_install_download: Download {zip} and unzip it somewhere you will not delete by accident.
guide_ext_install_open: Open chrome://extensions in the browser (brave://extensions on Brave, edge://extensions on Edge).
guide_ext_install_dev: Turn on Developer mode, the switch in the top right.
guide_ext_install_load: Click Load unpacked and pick the folder you unzipped.
guide_ext_install_pin: The aa mark lands in the toolbar. Pin it and the switches are one click away.
guide_ext_install_privacy: It collects nothing: no account, no analytics, no server, and nothing leaves the machine. What it stores and what it can see is written out on the {privacy}.
guide_ext_sites_body: Site by site, taken from the rule files, which are plain CSS with a header that says what each one hides and what it leaves alone.
guide_ext_x_gone_1: The For you tab on the home timeline
guide_ext_x_gone_3: The today's news box in the sidebar
guide_ext_x_stays_3: Search, and the Explore tab it lives behind
guide_ext_yt_gone_1: Every Shorts surface: the shelves on home, subscriptions, search and watch
guide_ext_yt_gone_2: The Shorts entry in both sidebars, and the Shorts tab on a channel
guide_ext_yt_gone_3: The /shorts/ player itself, which gets a short note in its place
guide_ext_ig_gone_1: Reels, and the Reels entry in the nav
guide_ext_ig_gone_2: The Explore grid and its tabs
guide_ext_ig_gone_3: The suggested for you blocks, in the sidebar and in the feed
guide_ext_ig_gone_4: The For you tab on the home feed
guide_ext_tt_gone_1: All of it. TikTok is a feed with a site drawn around it, so the page goes and a short note takes its place
guide_ext_switches_site: One switch per site in the popup. Off means the stylesheet is gone from that site, not that something is hiding behind a setting.
guide_ext_switches_master: One master switch over the four turns all of them off at once.
guide_ext_switches_custom: Custom CSS, on the options page, is the Stylus-shaped part: a domain, a block of CSS, applied on top of the built-in rules. Hide whatever bothers you on any other site.
guide_ext_switches_domain: A domain covers its subdomains, so reddit.com covers old.reddit.com.
guide_ext_switches_permission: A site outside the four asks the browser for access to that one site as you add the rule, once, and for nothing else.
guide_ext_switches_example_body: Say a news site keeps a trending sidebar next to the article. Open the browser's inspector, read the class off the element, and give the options page those two things.
